title: The Red Ball
summary: Max the dog loses his favorite ball in the park. Can he find it again?
teachingMethodReason: New vocabulary (dog, ball, park, tree, bench, flower) is presented through a simple communicative narrative, but the reader only reads and looks words up — there's no task with a real outcome for the reader to produce (so not TBL, per Willis 1996/Nunan 2006) and no other-subject content taught alongside the language (so not CLIL, per Coyle et al. 2010). That makes it classic Communicative Language Teaching: meaning-focused context over isolated drills.

pages.text: This is Max. Max is a {{dog}}. Max is {{happy}}.

vocab.definition: An animal that says woof and likes to play.
Feeling good, and smiling.

pages.text: Max has a {{ball}}. The ball is {{red}}. Max likes the ball.

vocab.definition: A round toy that you can throw, kick, or bounce.
A bright color, like an apple or a strawberry.

pages.text: Max runs in the {{park}}. He drops the ball. Where is the ball?

vocab.definition: A green place outside with grass and trees, where you can play.

pages.text: Max looks under a {{tree}}. He looks near the {{bench}}. No ball!

vocab.definition: A tall plant with a trunk, branches, and leaves.
A long seat for sitting outside.

pages.text: Max finds the ball next to a {{flower}}. Max is happy again! Woof, woof!

vocab.definition: A pretty plant that can smell nice and comes in many colors.

title: My Family
summary: Meet a happy family and learn simple words for the people you love.
teachingMethodReason: Family vocabulary (mother, father, sister, house, home) is delivered through a short communicative narrative with glossing. There's no task for the reader to complete (not TBL) and no cross-curricular content beyond the language itself (not CLIL), so this is CLT.

pages.text: This is my {{family}}. We live in a small {{house}}.

vocab.definition: The people you live with, like your parents and siblings.
A building where people live.

pages.text: This is my {{mother}}. She likes to read a {{book}}.

vocab.definition: Your mom, a parent.
Pages with words and pictures that you read.

pages.text: This is my {{father}}. He works at a {{table}}.

vocab.definition: Your dad, a parent.
A piece of furniture you eat or work on.

pages.text: This is my {{sister}}. She has a {{cat}}.

vocab.definition: A girl who has the same parents as you.
A small furry pet that says meow.

pages.text: I love my family. We are happy at {{home}}.

vocab.definition: The place where you live with your family.

title: A Day at the Park
summary: Mia and Tom spend a sunny day playing, exploring, and making a new furry friend.
teachingMethodReason: A recount-style narrative that builds everyday communicative vocabulary in context; no task outcome for the reader and no subject content beyond English, so CLT rather than TBL or CLIL. Note: its lost-ball-over-the-fence beat is structurally close to a TBL problem-solving task (Willis, 1996) — a prompt asking the reader to guess where the ball landed before the reveal would make it genuinely TBL.

pages.text: Yesterday, Mia and Tom went to the park. It was a sunny day, so they were very {{excited}}.

vocab.definition: Feeling very happy and full of energy about something.

pages.text: First, they played with a red ball under a big tree. Tom kicked the ball, and it flew over the {{fence}}!

vocab.definition: A wall made of wood or metal around a garden or field.

pages.text: Mia {{climbed}} over the fence to find the ball. She found it next to some yellow flowers.

vocab.definition: Went up or over something using your hands and feet.

pages.text: Then, they sat on a bench and ate their lunch. They had {{sandwiches}} and juice.

vocab.definition: Food made of bread with something tasty inside.
A meal you eat in the middle of the day.

pages.text: A little dog came near them. It wanted a {{piece}} of their sandwich! Mia gave it a small piece.

vocab.definition: A small part of something.

pages.text: Before they went home, Mia and Tom watched the clouds and talked about their {{favorite}} animals. It was a {{wonderful}} day.

vocab.definition: The one you like best.
Very good; amazing.

title: The Mystery of the Missing Cat
summary: When Anna's cat vanishes, she and her friend Ben follow the clues to solve the mystery.
teachingMethodReason: The characters solve a problem, but the reader doesn't: per Willis (1996)/Nunan (2006), TBL requires the learner to use language to reach a real outcome themselves (e.g. listing clues, predicting the cat's location), which this text doesn't ask for yet — so it's CLT today, not TBL. It's the strongest candidate in the library to convert to genuine TBL: add a task like 'Where do you think Whiskers is? List two places to check' before the page 5 reveal, and it would qualify.

pages.text: Anna's cat, Whiskers, {{disappeared}} on Monday morning. She {{searched}} the house but couldn't find him anywhere.

vocab.definition: Suddenly could not be seen; went missing.
Looked carefully for something.

pages.text: Anna decided to {{investigate}}. She grabbed a magnifying glass and started looking for {{clues}} in the garden.

vocab.definition: To try to find out the truth about something.
Small pieces of information that help solve a mystery.

pages.text: She {{noticed}} some paw prints near the fence. If Whiskers had gone this way, he might be in the {{neighbor's}} yard.

vocab.definition: Saw or became aware of something.
Belonging to the person who lives next door.

pages.text: Anna's friend Ben {{joined}} the search. Together, they {{followed}} the paw prints all the way to an old tree.

vocab.definition: Came together with someone to do something.
Went after or behind something.

pages.text: {{Suddenly}}, they heard a soft meow coming from above. Whiskers was stuck in the tree, looking a little {{embarrassed}}!

vocab.definition: Happening quickly and without warning.
Feeling shy or awkward about something.

pages.text: Ben climbed up {{carefully}} and brought Whiskers down. Anna hugged her cat tightly, {{relieved}} that the mystery was finally {{solved}}.

vocab.definition: Doing something with a lot of attention, to avoid mistakes.
Feeling calm again after being worried.
Found the answer to a problem.
